text:
Josh Norris needed Friday. Two goals against Columbus, both set up by Zach Benson, ended a stretch that had The Hockey Writers saying he needed to justify his place in the lineup. Buffalo Hockey Beat called it breaking out of a slump, and The Athletic's Matthew Fairburn wrote about what allowed him to break through.

Our numbers say the slump was never really his. Norris has 4 goals on 3.29 expected, a touch ahead of schedule. The problem is everyone else: Buffalo has scored 10.0 fewer goals than its chances deserve with Norris on the ice, the biggest gap on this team, and the Sabres control 52% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him. That's a center doing the work and getting a single assist for it.

He plays his 300th NHL game Sunday against Vegas. At 27, after an injury-heavy run in Ottawa and a trade to Buffalo, the scoring touch that produced 104 career goals before this season is clearly still there. We project about 41 points. If the line's luck turns even halfway, he'll beat that.
headline: Josh Norris breaks through
